body.statement: For every \(N\ge4\) and every bounded empirical marginal triple \(F\), there exists \(T\in\mathcal S_N(F)\) with average cost at most \(V_{\mathrm{rel}}(F)+3456/N\); therefore \(V_{\mathrm{int}}(F)-V_{\mathrm{rel}}(F)\le\min\{1/4,3456/N\}\). If the atoms and an optimal coupling \(\pi^\star\) are rational, \(\mathsf A_{\mathrm{round}}\) returns such a schedule, equivalently two permutations relative to arm 1, in time polynomial in \(N\) and the rational input bit length. The vertex extraction, comparisons, and output use exact rational arithmetic.
body.justification: The theorem supplies an explicit same-population-size implementation guarantee rather than denominator-clearing replication or an arbitrary vanishing error.
body.gap: Emami and Pass (2025, Discussion) ask for quantitative Monge approximation, and Haus (2015) supplies bottleneck approximations; neither proves a uniform additive same-empirical-marginal squared-cost rate with bit-polynomial construction.
body.consumer: A trial analyst can turn a fractional transport optimum into one realizable \(N\)-unit potential-outcome completion with an auditable deterministic error.
body.proof_tex:
Apply def:rounding-algorithm and lem:hierarchical-repair to an optimal coupling \(\pi^\star\).  The output \(T_{\mathrm{alg}}\) lies in \(\mathcal S_N(F)\), and lem:quadratic-slack-accounting gives
\[
 C_{\mathrm{alg}}(F)<V_{\mathrm{rel}}(F)+\frac{3456}{N}.
\]
Every realizable schedule induces a coupling in \(\Gamma(F)\), while \(T_{\mathrm{alg}}\) is feasible for def:realizable-value.  Hence
\[
 V_{\mathrm{rel}}(F)\le V_{\mathrm{int}}(F)
 \le C_{\mathrm{alg}}(F)
 <V_{\mathrm{rel}}(F)+\frac{3456}{N}.
\]
Also \(0\le C(y)\le1/4\), because \(\sum_ac_ay_a\in[-1/2,1/2]\).  It follows that
\[
 0\le V_{\mathrm{int}}(F)-V_{\mathrm{rel}}(F)
 \le\min\left\{\frac14,\frac{3456}{N}\right\}.
\]

For the complexity assertion, let the rational input bit length be \(B\).  Aggregating and sorting at most \(N\) atoms per arm is polynomial.  The support \(E\) has at most \(N^3\) cells, and each \(G_{as}\) is obtained by scanning that support.  The separation argument in lem:hierarchical-repair gives \(L=O(B)\), and dyadic cell indices are computed directly from rational endpoints rather than by materializing a grid.

At each depth the basic-table step is implemented by the support-elimination construction in lem:hierarchical-repair.  Rational Gaussian elimination supplies an integral kernel vector after clearing denominators; its coordinates are minors of a zero--one matrix and therefore have polynomial bit length by the Leibniz determinant bound.  If the current table has common denominator \(D\), one elimination multiplies a common denominator by at most one such kernel coordinate.  There are at most \(N^3\) eliminations per depth, so the accumulated bit length is polynomial in \(N+B\).  Exact rational addition, multiplication, comparison, and Gaussian elimination consequently give polynomial bit complexity.  Freezing expands at most \(N\) rows.  The three tree matchings use at most \(O(NL)\) occurrence moves.  Thus the whole deterministic construction is polynomial in \(N\) and \(B\).

Finally, label the output rows by their arm-1 occurrences.  Since each output column has exactly the prescribed occurrence multiset, the arm-2 and arm-3 occurrence labels define two permutations relative to arm 1, including when values repeat.  This proves every part of the theorem for rational input; the preceding finite construction and inequalities use only order and finite-dimensional feasibility, and therefore give existence for arbitrary real atoms as well.
